title: Giants on the Frontier - Nightstone Chapter 1 scaffold
tagline: A local-play scaffold for your owned Chapter 1 notes: Nightstone, the missing villagers, the caves, and the strange giant tower.
sourceNote: Not official WotC content. Paraphrased play scaffold only; use your owned book/PDF for boxed text, maps, exact room keys, treasure, and stat blocks.
campaignGuide: Run Chapter 1 as an investigation of an abandoned village after a giant attack. Do not invent a welcoming leader at the gate. Nightstone is quiet except for a ringing bell; the drawbridge is down; the palisade entrance is open; the keep and bridge show major impact damage; the central megalith is missing from the village square. The survivors fled toward nearby caves and were captured by goblins. Goblins have entered the abandoned village to loot it. Use the owner's PDF for exact read-aloud, maps, room details, and named treasure. Log important discoveries as canon facts.

settlement-arrival.goal: Approach Nightstone and recognize that the settlement is abandoned and damaged.
settlement-arrival.starter: A bell rings somewhere inside Nightstone. The road ends at a lowered drawbridge over the moat, with no guards answering from the open palisade gate.
settlement-arrival.guidance: Paraphrase the approach from the owner's PDF. Establish the moat, wooden palisade, open gate, silent village, visible windmill and steeple, and the damaged keep across the water. No leader, guards, or villagers greet the party. If the player greets someone, answer with silence, the bell, and environmental details. Perception or Investigation DC 10-13 can confirm no ordinary village activity and signs of a recent evacuation or attack. Use advance_scene once the party enters or commits to investigating inside.

village-square.goal: Discover the missing nightstone and evidence of a giant bombardment.
village-square.starter: Inside the palisade, the village square is scarred by fallen rocks. A conspicuous empty space marks where a great stone once stood.
village-square.guidance: Keep this as investigation, not a social briefing. Reveal that a large central megalith is gone, buildings were struck from above, and the inhabitants appear to have fled rather than formed a defense. Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Perception can identify useful clues. Do not provide exact boxed text or room keys; point the user to their PDF for map areas and treasure.

ringing-bell.goal: Trace the bell and learn that the noise is not a normal alarm response.
ringing-bell.starter: The bell keeps ringing from the village chapel, too steady and lonely to sound like an organized warning.
ringing-bell.guidance: The bell should feel like an eerie clue, not a summons from authorities. If the party calls out, no village leader answers. Use cautious exploration and simple checks to reveal whether creatures or hazards are nearby. Use advance_scene once the party understands the bell is part of the abandoned-village mystery.

goblin-looters.goal: Confront goblin looters in the abandoned village and learn where the villagers went.
goblin-looters.starter: Small figures dart between damaged buildings with stolen goods clutched in their arms.
goblin-looters.guidance: Run this as goblin looters exploiting the empty village after the giant attack. The party can fight, intimidate, trick, or capture them. A captured or frightened goblin can reveal that villagers fled to nearby caves and were captured there. Log that lead as a canon fact. Use advance_scene after the goblin scene resolves and the cave lead is established.

cave-leads.goal: Follow evidence from Nightstone toward the caves where the villagers fled.
cave-leads.starter: Tracks lead away from Nightstone toward the hills: hurried villagers, small goblin prints, and signs of a forced march.
cave-leads.guidance: This scene connects Nightstone to the cave rescue. Survival, Perception, Insight, or Intimidation can establish the cave route and likely opposition. Keep the route summary concise and use the owner's PDF for exact travel and cave details. Use advance_scene when the party reaches the cave entrance.

dripping-caves.goal: Rescue the captured villagers from goblins and their stronger allies.
dripping-caves.starter: The cave mouth smells of damp stone, smoke, and unwashed bodies. Voices echo from deeper chambers.
dripping-caves.guidance: Use this as a compact rescue version of the Dripping Caves. The villagers are prisoners, goblins control the caves, and stronger brute-force allies may be present. For solo play, reduce enemy pressure, allow stealth/social solutions, and do not force every cave area. Log rescued survivors and any named NPCs the user chooses from the PDF. Use advance_scene after the villagers are rescued or the party secures a clear outcome.

tower-of-zephyros.goal: Meet a strange giant ally and establish the next phase of the giant crisis.
tower-of-zephyros.starter: After Nightstone's crisis, an enormous floating tower becomes the party's unlikely road onward.
tower-of-zephyros.guidance: Treat this as the transition from Nightstone into the broader giant story. Use the owner's PDF for the giant NPC's exact personality and tower events. The key function is to give the party transport, foreshadow giant politics, and move toward the next chapter location. Use advance_scene when the party accepts the next destination.

endingMessage: Nightstone's immediate crisis is resolved. Record who was rescued, what the party learned about the giant attack, and where the tower carries them next.

npcs.name: Nightstone survivor
npcs.description: A rescued villager or named NPC chosen from the owner's PDF.
knowledge: The village was struck from above before the survivors fled.
The villagers took shelter in nearby caves and were captured there.

npcs.name: Captured goblin
npcs.description: A frightened looter who knows where the villagers were taken.
knowledge: Goblins came to loot the abandoned village after the attack.
The cave captives are under control of the goblin band.

mock.socialSuccess: The survivor explains what they saw and points the party toward the next lead.
mock.socialFailure: The survivor is shaken and gives only fragments until the party earns trust.
mock.explorationSuccess: You find a solid clue: Nightstone was struck from above, its people fled, and the next trail leads toward the caves.
mock.explorationFailure: The silence, bell, and broken buildings confirm danger, but the exact sequence remains unclear. Try another angle or move deeper into the village.
mock.canonFactOnSocialSuccess: Nightstone survivors fled toward nearby caves after the attack.
